newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare rise but end up on Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare rise but end up on Q2 earnings.

text.p: Mexican shares trimmed some of their earlier gains on intraday profit-taking, but nonetheless ended up on Thursday on positive market reaction to second quarter company earnings, dealers and analysts said.
"Companies seem to have posted good earnings and there are players who find prices very attractive," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst with the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 20.53 points, or 0.43 percent, at 4,762.65, after earlier trading as high as 4,807.58.
Dealers noted trading volume was average at 88.4 million shares and inflation data released in late trade had little impact on dealing.
"The bourse pared its gains for no other reason than local day-trippers taking profits, as there was little international money," a desk trader said.
"Inflation was in line with expectations and did not affect things one way or the other," he added.
Banco de Mexico announced in late trade the Consumer Price Index had risen by 0.48 percent for July 1-15, compared with an average 0.49-percent rise predicted in a Reuters survey.

Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) contributed most to market gains, dealers said and ended up 32 centavos at 20.20 pesos, off an earlier high of 20.40. The market bought Telmex on earnings it posted late on Tuesday, they added.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced sliders by 62 to 37 out of 120 stocks that changed hands during the session.
